title: SRE operational logbook — July 6-10 2026
content:
SRE operational logbook — week of Mon Jul 6 to Fri Jul 10, 2026

TL;DR:
- Three customer-visible incidents this week; two resolved with mitigation, one escalated to infra-engineering for a systemic fix.
- SLOs: availability dipped below target for one endpoint (model-serve-ingress) during a cache storm; P95 latency spike observed for short sequences (<=64 tokens).
- On-call handoff checklist updated with clearer PV diagnostics and a new pager policy for multi-region fallbacks.

Attendees (standup / warroom snippets):
- Aisha (on-call), Miguel (runtime), Claire (networking), Devon (observability), Priya (infra)
- Ad-hoc: product eng lead (for customer escalations), solutions-eng for customer comms

Incident summaries:
1) Incident: transient multi-region cache evictions -> model-serve latency spike (SEV2)
   - Start: 2026-07-07 02:14 UTC, End: 2026-07-07 03:03 UTC
   - Symptoms: P95 increased from 120ms -> 620ms for model-serve-ingress across us-west-2 and eu-west-1. Error rate (5xx) briefly rose to 1.2%.
   - Customer impact: A subset of real-time inference customers experienced increased latency and a small number of timeouts. No data leakage.
   - Immediate mitigation: forced warm caches via controlled synthetic requests; increased cache size on hot-prefix nodes; temporarily routed new traffic to dedicated pool in us-east-1 for impacted routers.
   - Root cause (hypothesis): eviction storm triggered by a background retrain process that invalidated large prefix sets concurrently with cache compaction. Sequence: training job bumped model weights, cache invalidation event was batched and applied during peak requests.
   - Owners: Miguel (diagnostics), Priya (prevent recurrence / infra change), Claire (routing policy tweaks)
   - Linked ticket: SRE-324 (postmortem + follow-ups)
   - Follow-ups: add jitter to cache invalidation propagation, integrate invalidation window with autoscaling windows, add targeted warmup job post-invalidation. Due 2026-07-22.

2) Incident: ingress rate-limiter misconfiguration causing throttled requests (SEV3)
   - Start: 2026-07-08 11:05 UTC, End: 2026-07-08 11:45 UTC
   - Symptoms: spikes in 429s for a small number of noisy API keys; correlation with a config rollout that reduced per-key token bucket size for a micro-segment.
   - Mitigation: rolled back config, reverted rollout in 11 minutes via Canary rollback, increased guardrails for future rollouts.
   - Owner: Claire (networking)
   - Follow-ups: add pre-flight dry-run for rate-limiter config changes, add automatic escalation if rollback threshold hit twice. Ticket SRE-330.

3) Incident: storage-tier throttling -> RPC timeouts for background writes (SEV3, internal)
   - Start: 2026-07-09 04:20 UTC, End: 2026-07-09 06:50 UTC
   - Symptoms: internal batch jobs and checkpoint writes observed increased retry/backoff; not customer-visible except delayed cache warms.
   - Mitigation: shifted background checkpointing to lower-priority queue, throttled ingestion for internal backlog, engaged storage provider support for transient throttling.
   - Owner: Devon (observability) + Priya (infra)
   - Follow-ups: add explicit write-rate throttling in the runtime, surface storage throttling metrics to main SRE dashboard.

SLO snapshot (end-of-week numbers):
- model-serve-ingress availability (target 99.95%): 99.88% (incident 1 was the majority cause)
- P95 latency for short sequences (target <=150ms): 210ms week aggregate, P95 during incident 620ms
- 5xx rate (target <=0.1%): weekly avg 0.18% (spike during incidents)
- Notes: trending issue is cache warmup strategy after invalidations; this has direct visible impact on P95 and availability for bursty workloads.

On-call handoff notes (from night -> day shift; added to runbook):
- Active incidents: none at handoff (2026-07-10 08:00 UTC).
- Outstanding tasks carried over:
  * Finish instrumentation for cache invalidation window (owner: Miguel) — status: prototyping, tracking in SRE-324.
  * Implement pre-flight checks for rate-limiter changes (owner: Claire) — status: design doc needed.
  * Dashboard card for storage throttling (owner: Devon) — status: sprint queue.
- Checkpoint: verify on-call phone and escalation matrix; confirmed.
- Quick triage checklist appended:
  1) Check region SLO dashboard (link in linked_artifacts)
  2) Inspect recent deploys in last 45m: `infra-deploy-service` and `rate-limiter`
  3) Run `sre/diag/cache-heatmap --last 60m` (local helper)
  4) If P95 > 300ms and 5xx rising, fire a bridge AND consider temporary routing to backup pool.

Runbook and process changes proposed:
- Add "cache-invalidation window" to the deployment checklist for any model/weight update.
- New config gating for rate-limiter: require dry-run and observed 0.0% 429 increase in canary for at least 15 minutes before global rollout.
- Add a small synthetic warmup (low-cost) that runs for 5 minutes post-invalidation targeted at the top-100 prefixes.

Observability notes:
- Missing metric observed: cache-invalidation-batch-size (instrumentation gap). Adding metric + alert to prevent unbounded invalidation bursts.
- Dashboard improvements: create a combined "cache health" card that shows hit-rate, eviction-rate, and warmup-traffic per-region. Owner: Devon.

Action items (owner — due):
- Miguel — instrument invalidation window + initial dashboard (due 2026-07-15)
- Priya — coordinate infra change to allow staged invalidation propagation (due 2026-07-22)
- Claire — design pre-flight checks for rate-limiter config rollouts (due 2026-07-18)
- Devon — add storage throttling card and alert (due 2026-07-16)
- Aisha — draft customer-facing incident summary for impacted tenants (due 2026-07-12)

Retrospective notes / questions to resolve:
- How do we balance aggressive cache invalidation for consistency vs. availability for real-time customers?
- Should we introduce a "soft invalidation" mode where old entries expire naturally for 30s before being purged? Pros/cons to evaluate.
- Can the serving runtime perform on-the-fly warming for top-k prefixes without large cost? Cost tradeoff analysis required.

Meeting notes (SRE weekly sync — 2026-07-10)
- Decisions made:
  * Approve work to add jittered invalidation propagation and warmup job (Priya + Miguel).
  * Require rate-limiter dry-run gating for future rollouts (Claire to own).
- Open: estimate for warmup cost and expected reduction in P95 — action item to run small experiment (Aisha + solutions-eng)

Notes to self / rough thoughts (informal):
- Need quick script that can rehydrate the top-100 prefixes from recent traffic logs — might save an hour during incidents.
- Consider adding a small reserve of warm instances in each region that can be spun up in <60s (warm-pool). Tradeoff: cost vs. tail latency.
- When drafting customer comms, emphasize mitigation steps and expected timeline for systemic fix. Keep message short and proactive.

Attachments / artifacts to link in final postmortem:
- SRE-324 (cache eviction postmortem draft)
- infra PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/456 (warmup job prototype)
- Slack warroom thread: https://app.slack.com/client/T12345/C67890/thread/1623456789.000200

End of logbook entry.

-- Aisha
